A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSH-Bench work and are readable throughout. Pages 2–20 have identical text and rendered content. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains the supplementary sections cited in the text, so no separate appendix content is available to compare.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original evaluations of 19 generation models, human-alignment measurements for SICS, and analyses by subject category, difficulty and prompt scenario.

after.justification: The same original empirical results remain in Tables 1–3 and Figures 7–8, including model evaluations and SICS human-alignment measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same benchmark construction pipeline, difficulty/scenario classification and SICS model procedure. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both retain 459 subject images, 58 categories, 5,508 prompts, three difficulty levels and six prompt scenarios. DreamBench and DreamBench++ comparisons in Table 2 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within Tables 1–3, including the CLIP, DINO and GPT-4o metric comparisons and the generation-model leaderboard.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation settings are identical, including SICS, CLIP-T and HPSv2 metrics, score normalization, annotation procedures and final-score weights.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Figure 8 retain the same category, difficulty and scenario analyses. The qualitative comparisons in Figures 2 and 7 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Table 1's Kendall and Spearman correlations. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing information is added or removed.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results, rankings and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains SICS's overall Kendall correlation of 0.677, and Table 3 retains Nano-Banana's final score of 0.272.

T1.justification: The final-score definition in Equation 1 is identical. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical subject coverage, difficulty/scenario diagnosis and SICS's efficiency and human alignment.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–5 preserve the same interpretations concerning benchmark difficulty, preservation/following tradeoffs and weaknesses on complex subjects and prompt scenarios. No applicability boundaries or limitations are revised.

D1.justification: The SICS training description, five-annotator setup, use of official implementations and code/data release statements are unchanged. The removed title-page emails are general author contacts, not technical access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning passages and all 76 bibliography entries are identical. No cited work or novelty relationship changes.

P1.justification: On page 1, 'Tencent' and the author email line are replaced by 'No Institute Given'; the arXiv version/date stamp also changes. Author names, substantive prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shorter affiliation block slightly shifts Figure 1, its caption and the abstract upward. Figure content is unchanged, and pages 2–20 retain identical layouts, figures and tables.

improvement.justification: The revision changes only title-page information and spacing; methods, evidence, interpretations and substantive exposition remain identical. Removing the affiliation and emails slightly reduces front-matter completeness but does not meaningfully alter the paper's overall research quality.
